Lessons.Title: Solve Problems with Multiplication and Division
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will practice solving multi-step problems using all operations.
In the previous lesson, you solved word problems involving multiplicative comparison. In this lesson, you practice solving a wider variety of problems, with a focus on the relationships among multiple quantities in a situation. You think about how to represent the relationships with one or multiple equations and using multiple operations.

2021 source activity sequence: Warm-up: Number Talk: Divide by 8 (10 minutes); Activity 1: Two Truths and a Lie, or Two Lies and a Truth? (15 minutes); Activity 2: Buses for a Field Trip (20 minutes); Cool-down: To and Fro (5 minutes)
Math focus: Represent all given constraints in a multi-step operation, and interpret division remainders for resources like buses or tickets.

Worked Edulytics example: A 53-story building has one 17-ft floor and 52 other 11-ft stories. Calculate 17 + (52 × 11) = 589 ft. Use the total to verify the truth of the original source claim. For groups of people, round up nonzero remainders when every person needs a seat.
First-party Edulytics Cool-down (publisher's original not inspected): Forty-nine students need buses with 20 seats each. How many buses?
Original models, source figures, student-authored problems and teacher-scored explanations require separate academic review.

2021 source warm-up Number Talk Divide by 8: 848÷8=106 and 4,848÷8=606. Original first truth-test: 53-story building, first floor 17 feet, remaining 52 floors each 11 feet, so 17+52×11=589 feet: the stated 589-feet height is TRUE. Other source situations need their complete text before any truth labels.

Original Buses for a Field Trip: 375 people, 27-seat small buses at Company A or 48-seat large buses at Company B. If using ONLY one type, 14 small buses are needed (13×27=351<375, 14×27=378); or 8 large buses (7×48=336<375, 8×48=384). Remainders represent people still needing seats, so ROUND UP counts rather than dropping them. If the full publisher task permits mixing bus companies or includes extra cost constraints, teacher evaluates those separately.

Digital Practice REUSE existing G4 U06 contextual remainder decisions and multi-step context families as supportive independent questions. These do not claim exact 2021 business data, specific field-trip choices, or teacher source task parity.

WorkedExamples.Title: Source bus capacities, one company at a time
WorkedExamples.Question: How many 27-seat buses or 48-seat buses cover 375 passengers if all buses are the same size?
WorkedExamples.Method: Divide passengers by seats and round up for a nonzero remainder.
WorkedExamples.Check: Grounded in 2021 source passenger and seat counts; excludes unverified extra conditions.

WorkedExamples.Title: Source high-rise claim
WorkedExamples.Question: 53 floors: first 17 feet, 52 remaining at 11 feet. Is stated height 589 feet correct?
WorkedExamples.Method: Multiply remaining floors and add first floor.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Yes, the original Situation A height is correct.
WorkedExamples.Check: Only Situation A is shown in retained original excerpt.
